title: Form actions, and progressive enhancement that works with JavaScript off

videos.script:
This is the lesson the course was built around. {{off}} First, switch JavaScript off and look at the planner. You can read it. You cannot change a thing.

Then the server learns to save. {{saving}} One file, written so that two requests at once cannot lose a change.

Then a form action. {{action}} A plain HTML form, sent by the browser on its own, and a function on the server that receives it. It answers with a redirect, so that reloading the page never sends the form twice.

Then what happens when the form is wrong. {{fail}} The browser checks first. The server checks again, because anything can send a form.

Then a second form, for marking a session done. {{named}} And then the week moves into the address. {{week}} Every link, every form and every redirect can carry it, and the server can render it.

Only at the end does JavaScript come back. {{enhance}} One attribute, and the same forms work without a reload. Everything before it still works when the script never arrives. That is progressive enhancement.
